title: Surgical traffic remediation and staged rollback playbook for mixed-hosted/dedicated cross-region routing incidents
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Summary: Create a prescriptive, low-risk runbook and playbook for repairing misrouted traffic and KV-cache divergence that can occur during cross-region traffic shifts involving mixed Hosted + Dedicated customers. This ticket focuses on: tenant-aware surgical remediation, staged rollback commands, validation checks, safe fallbacks to compatible model variants, and coordinated customer communication. Scope includes Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and coordination instructions for Private/VPC customers when operator action is needed. Excludes lower-severity non-tenant-isolating issues.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook tested end-to-end in staging with simulated tenant traffic and at least two fault modes (regional network partition, autoscaler misplacement). 2) Clear command snippets for tenant pinning, partial region drain, and staged rollback validated by SRE run. 3) Communication templates approved by support & AMs. 4) Telemetry queries for correctness and SLA impact added to dashboards. 5) Postmortem checklist ready and linked.
steps: Step 0 - Triage: Confirm incident type with oncall: Is this a cross-region routing anomaly affecting layer-7 routing or a backend KV-consistency issue in replicas? Capture symptoms: elevated 5xx, increased tail latency, per-tenant error spikes, KV-miss ratio. Note affected tenants and dedicated pools.

Step 1 - Freeze automation: Immediately disable autoscale-based migrations and any scheduled traffic rebalances for the affected regions via infra flags (infra-toggle:regional-rebalance=false). Record toggles in incident log.

Step 2 - Tenant pinning (if tenant-specific degradation): For each affected tenant, apply a routing pin to healthy region via routing-api: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant}/pin with body {region: 'us-west-2', mode: 'sticky', ttl: 3600}. Use dedicated routing key for Dedicated customers. Document commands used and TTL values.

Step 3 - Surgical traffic siphon: Gradually mirror 5-10% of affected tenant requests to candidate region for validation while leaving primary routing intact (traffic-siphon window = 10m). Monitor error and latency delta. If delta < SLO threshold, increase to 25%, then 50%.

Step 4 - KV cache reconciliation: If KV-desync suspected, run KV-snapshot on primary then apply incremental patch to standby: run tooling kv-sync --src-region=us-east-1 --dst-region=us-west-2 --tenants=tenant-list --max-ops=5000. If snapshot latency impacts runtime, run in background with lower op rate and enable read-repair heuristics.

Step 5 - Canary model variant fallback: If model variant incompatibility or latency spike traced to a specific quantization profile, switch only the pinned tenants to a lower-latency variant using model-router: /v1/routes/update with filters {tenants:[...], variant: 'quant-8b'}. Avoid global variant switches.

Step 6 - Progressive region drain: For a region-level failover, perform staged draining: 1) mark region read-only for new dedicated allocations; 2) shift new session establishment to standby region; 3) after 15m, divert 50% of new and 25% of in-progress completions; 4) full traffic cutover after stability window.

Step 7 - Customer comms and AM coordination: Immediately notify affected customers via template (see communication_templates). For Dedicated customers include estimated remediation ETA and whether a live migration is required. For Private customers, provide operator actions and a timeboxed maintenance window.

Step 8 - Validation and rollback gate: Maintain verification checks for 30m after each major step. If any check fails (per-tenant error rate > 2x baseline or USL latency breach), trigger rollback_commands for the last change and escalate to SE oncall.
Step 9 - Post-incident follow-up: Run postmortem checklist, record root cause hypothesis, corrective actions (code/infra/ops), and schedule a DR drill for the new runbook within next cycle.

Step 10 - Automate safe-guards: Create a follow-up ticket to add guardrails: automatic read-only during KV-syncs, tenant-level circuit-breaker thresholds, and telemetry alerts for unusual cross-region request ratios.
verification_checks: API health: 200/5xx ratio back to baseline for affected tenants across 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
Latency: P95 and P99 for pinned tenants within SLO (P95 < 120ms hosted, < 200ms dedicated) over a 10-minute window.
KV correctness: sample key compare between regions % mismatch < 0.01% after sync.
Model output stability: fuzz-similarity score for mirrored requests > 0.9 compared to baseline.
No new customer tickets created in 60 minutes for the same issue after remediation steps.
Dashboard: Traffic routing ratio to regions shows expected shift and no unexpected spikes in other regions.
Smoke testing: Run synthetic prompt set for top 10 affected tenants, verify completion and structured output validity.
rollback_commands: Routing rollback: POST /v1/routes/rollback with body {operation_id: <last-op>, force: true}
Tenant unpin: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant}/unpin to restore normal routing TTL expiry.
KV revert: kv-sync --reverse --src-region=<standby> --dst-region=<primary> --max-ops=2000 (only for emergency revert under SRE approval).
Model variant rollback: model-router: /v1/variants/set with filters {tenants:[...], variant: 'stable-previous'}
Autoscale re-enable: infra-toggle:regional-rebalance=true after confirmation from infra lead.
telemetry_queries: Per-tenant error spike: SELECT tenant, sum(errors) FROM metrics.requests WHERE region IN (...) AND timestamp > now()-15m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY sum(errors) DESC LIMIT 50
Cross-region ratio: SELECT region, count(*) FROM routing.requests WHERE timestamp > now()-10m GROUP BY region
KV-miss-rate: SELECT region, avg(kv_miss) FROM metrics.kv WHERE tenant IN (...) AND timestamp > now()-30m GROUP BY region
Tail-latency: SELECT percentile(latency, 95), percentile(latency, 99) FROM metrics.latencies WHERE tenant=... AND time>now()-10m
Model-diff: Compare inference outputs for mirrored requests using similarity score pipeline stored in evals-runner: fetch last 200 pairs and compute average fuzz similarity.
communication_templates: Initial inbound (internal): Incident declared: Cross-region routing anomaly affecting tenants [X,Y,Z]. Impact: elevated 5xx and increased latency. Current action: pinning affected tenants to healthy region and starting KV reconciliation. SRE lead: <name>. Estimated ETA: 45-90 minutes. See runbook ENG-32011.

Customer facing (support/AM): Short: We are investigating an infrastructure routing issue impacting requests in [region]. We have applied targeted mitigations for your account and will update within 60 minutes with ETA. Long: We are performing tenant-specific routing and data integrity checks. No data loss is expected. If you prefer a manual migration window, please reply and we’ll arrange a dedicated migration with minimal downtime.

Status update (30m): Actions taken: pinned traffic, started safe KV-sync, mirrored 10% traffic for validation. Current metrics: error rate reduced by 45%. Next update in 30 minutes or earlier if conditions change.
